title: Counterfactual Co-op: A Time-Machine for First-Years
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: radical-reinterpretation (probability 0.05)
Title: Counterfactual Co-op: A Time-Machine for First-Years
Thesis: Show first-years their own probable sophomore year twice — brand-only vs balanced — using anonymized NUworks alumni trajectories, delivered as a Power BI story in Teams.
Why this frame: Brand fixation is a forecasting failure, not an information failure; NUworks already holds five years of placement outcomes that can render each student's near-future side-by-side, which is a far more visceral intervention than another job digest.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Sam Chen
  Role: First-year Industrial Engineering student, College of Engineering
  Context: Six weeks into fall semester. Has submitted 12 applications — all to Google, Tesla, SpaceX, Apple, and Goldman. Zero applications to SMEs. Spends evenings refreshing application portals and lurking in r/cscareerquestions. Has never heard of any of the 340 SMEs hiring through NUworks this cycle.
  Emotional state: Outwardly confident, privately anxious. Believes anything below a FAANG offer would embarrass his family. Hasn't told his advisor he's been ghosted 4x already.
  Pain points:
    - Cannot picture what a 'balanced' co-op search actually looks like in lived terms — only abstract advice from advisors
    - Has no peer reference frame; assumes everyone else is also chasing only brand names and succeeding
    - Search aperture is collapsing as rejections arrive — narrowing further into the same 5 companies
    - Doesn't trust generic 'consider smaller companies' messaging because it feels like consolation, not strategy
  JTBD: When I'm deciding which co-ops to apply to, I want to see what actually happens to students who chose like me, so I can make a bet I won't regret in 18 months.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Strategic Co-op Director (Liz's team): Defines what counts as a 'successful sophomore outcome' in the forecast model; reviews anonymization thresholds before launch.
  - Co-op Advisor: Receives shared forecasts from students; uses them as the opening artifact in 1:1 meetings instead of a blank-page conversation.
  - Data Systems Admin: Owns the NUworks → Power BI dataflow; enforces k-anonymity (k≥15) before any cohort is rendered.
  - FERPA Compliance Officer: Approves the anonymization disclosure copy and audits the dataflow quarterly.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Sam opens a Teams notification titled 'Two versions of your sophomore year, Sam.' He taps in. A cinematic split-screen Power BI story renders: 200 anonymized alumni who started his exact major, GPA band, and first-week application pattern — half went brand-only, half went balanced. He slides a portfolio mix dial from 100/0 to 60/40 and watches his projected sophomore-fall placement probability climb from 31% to 78%, with a real anonymized alum's trajectory animating alongside.

USE CASES (10) — the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. See Your Two Probable Futures
     Trigger: Sam receives a Teams card on Monday morning of week 6 — 'Sam, here are two versions of your sophomore year. Takes 4 minutes.'
     Flow: Sam taps the card → splash screen renders his name and major with two ghosted silhouettes ('Brand-Only Sam' and 'Balanced Sam') → he taps 'Show me' → split-screen Power BI canvas loads with placement rate, median offer, ghosting count, and time-to-offer for each cohort path.
     AI role: Cohort Outcome Forecaster matches Sam's first-week behavior vector against 5 years of anonymized NUworks alumni and renders the two most statistically distinct cohort trajectories.
     Outcome: Sam sees concrete numerical contrast — 31% vs 78% sophomore placement — for the first time, in his own terms, not generic advice.
  2. Explore the Brand-Only Cohort Outcome
     Trigger: Sam taps the left panel labeled 'Brand-Only — 104 alumni like you.'
     Flow: Panel expands → timeline animation runs from Sept Y1 to May Y2 → markers drop showing application volume (avg 47), rejection rate (89%), ghosting events (median 6), final placement type (31% any co-op, 4% brand-name co-op, 65% no fall placement).
     AI role: Counterfactual Narrative Writer generates 2-3 sentence summary of what this cohort's sophomore fall typically feels like, in plain language, without verbatim quotes.
     Outcome: Sam confronts the realistic distribution of his current strategy — including that even the brand-only winners are a 4% slice.
  3. Explore the Balanced-Portfolio Cohort Outcome
     Trigger: Sam taps the right panel labeled 'Balanced — 96 alumni like you.'
     Flow: Panel expands → same timeline runs → markers show application volume (avg 22), rejection rate (54%), ghosting events (median 2), final placement (78% any co-op, 23% at SMEs that became full-time offers by junior year).
     AI role: Counterfactual Narrative Writer describes the balanced cohort's experience and explicitly names which SME categories punched above their weight for industrial engineering majors.
     Outcome: Sam sees the balanced path isn't 'settling' — it has higher absolute brand-name conversion by junior year because of skills accumulated in SME roles.
  4. Read Three Anonymized Alumni Vignettes
     Trigger: Sam scrolls past the cohort dashboards into a 'Three people, three paths' carousel.
     Flow: Three vignettes render with synthetic names ('Alumni A', 'Alumni B', 'Alumni C'), each with a 4-frame timeline → industrial engineering peer 18 months ago → first co-op company type → what they learned → where they are now (Y3 spring).
     AI role: Alumni Vignette Synthesizer composes the vignettes from clustered anonymized records (k≥15 per cluster), never surfacing identifiable patterns, never reproducing any verbatim source quote.
     Outcome: Statistical patterns become human stories without violating FERPA — Sam feels he's reading peers, not data.
  5. Adjust Your Search Mix in Real Time
     Trigger: Sam taps the 'What if I shifted my mix?' CTA below the vignettes.
     Flow: Live Portfolio Mix Adjuster screen loads with a dial from 100% brand-name to 100% SME → Sam drags the dial → projected sophomore-fall placement rate, median offer, and ghosting count update with 240ms eased transitions → a small animated alumni avatar walks across a path that morphs with the dial.
     AI role: Portfolio Mix Recommender computes the conditional probability surface from the matched cohort and animates the gradient.
     Outcome: Sam discovers the inflection point is at roughly 55-65% brand-name, not 0% — the message is 'rebalance,' not 'abandon.'
  6. Watch Forecast Update Live
     Trigger: Sam continues sliding the dial past various mixes.
     Flow: Counter values tick smoothly → at 60/40, a confetti-restrained haptic-style flash highlights 78% → sensitivity bars appear showing which factors are driving the lift (SME application count, application diversity, time-to-first-application).
     AI role: Sensitivity Analysis Explainer surfaces in plain English which two or three input changes contributed most to the lift.
     Outcome: Sam understands causality, not just correlation — he can act on the specific levers.
  7. Share the Forecast With Your Advisor
     Trigger: Sam taps 'Share with my advisor' in the top right.
     Flow: Teams share sheet opens pre-addressed to his assigned advisor → Sam can add a note → the advisor receives an embedded Power BI report card plus Sam's commitment ('I'll apply to 4 SMEs this week').
     AI role: Claude drafts a one-sentence opener for Sam's note based on which insight surprised him most (inferred from dwell time).
     Outcome: The next advisor meeting opens with a shared artifact instead of a blank slate.
  8. Commit to a Weekly SME Quota
     Trigger: Sam taps 'Lock in my new mix.'
     Flow: A modal proposes 4 SME applications per week for 6 weeks → Sam confirms → a Power Automate flow schedules Friday Teams check-ins → each Friday, Sam gets a card showing his actual mix vs target with NUworks data refreshed nightly.
     AI role: Copilot agent recomputes Sam's forecast weekly with his real application data and nudges if he drifts back to brand-only.
     Outcome: Behavior change is locked into the cadence; the forecast becomes a longitudinal contract, not a one-time visualization.
  9. Revisit the Forecast Mid-Semester
     Trigger: Week 10 — Sam wants to see if his actual behavior has moved his projection.
     Flow: He reopens the Teams card → a 'You vs your week-6 forecast' overlay renders → his actual application mix sits at 70/30, projected placement now at 64% (up from his original 31%).
     AI role: Forecaster re-runs against current behavior; Narrative Writer flags the delta in encouraging but honest language.
     Outcome: Sam sees that the model is responsive to him, not deterministic — he feels agency.
  10. Advisor Pulls a Cohort-Wide View
     Trigger: Sam's advisor opens her Teams sidebar.
     Flow: She sees her caseload of 38 first-years → 11 are still in brand-only territory → she filters and bulk-sends them the Counterfactual experience.
     AI role: Power BI cohort detector flags students whose week-6 pattern resembles the high-risk brand-only cluster.
     Outcome: Advisor time is spent on the 11 who need it most, not generic outreach.

KEY SCREENS (10) — every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Two Futures Splash (Teams Card → Web View) — purpose: Hook Sam into a 4-minute experience by personalizing the proposition before any data appears.
     Primary element: Full-bleed split-screen with two ghosted silhouettes labeled 'Brand-Only Sam' and 'Balanced Sam,' his major and GPA band rendered in editorial serif.
     Motion character: Silhouettes breathe slowly (1.2s loop); a thin diagonal seam between them animates inward on tap.
  2. Cohort Outcome Comparison (Power BI Canvas) — purpose: Side-by-side rendering of the two probable sophomore years using real anonymized cohort data.
     Primary element: Two stacked dashboards: placement rate gauge, application volume bar, ghosting count, median offer, time-to-offer. NUworks data-source badge bottom-left.
     Motion character: Numbers count up over 900ms with easing; gauges sweep in counter-rotation; the dividing seam is a soft 1px rule, no harsh contrast.
  3. Alumni Vignette Carousel — purpose: Translate statistical clusters into three human-scale narratives without any identifying data.
     Primary element: Three editorial cards with synthetic monograms (A, B, C), a 4-frame horizontal timeline per card, and a FERPA anonymization seal.
     Motion character: Cards slide with parallax depth (background lags 30%); tapping a frame zooms it with a 280ms scale-and-fade.
  4. Live Portfolio Mix Adjuster — purpose: Let Sam manipulate the input variable (brand-name share) and watch outcomes update live — the headline aha moment.
     Primary element: Large horizontal dial from 100% brand → 100% SME, with three live counters above (Placement %, Median Offer, Ghosting). Walking alumni avatar below traverses a morphing path.
     Motion character: Dial has subtle resistance haptic feel via micro-bounces; counters tween over 240ms; the avatar's path morphs as a Bezier interpolation.
  5. Sensitivity Drilldown — purpose: Show Sam which specific levers move the forecast, not just that it moves.
     Primary element: Horizontal lever bars labeled 'SME applications,' 'Application diversity,' 'Time-to-first-application,' each with a contribution percentage and plain-English caption.
     Motion character: Bars fill left-to-right in sequence (stagger 80ms each); captions fade in beneath after the bar settles.
  6. Underlying NUworks Data Map — purpose: Honor the user's direction — show the actual NUworks → Power Automate → Azure OpenAI → Power BI dataflow, with k-anonymity gates visible.
     Primary element: Annotated dataflow diagram: NUworks tables (Placements, Employers, Students) → Power Automate connector → anonymization gate (k≥15) → Power BI dataset → Teams delivery. Each node clickable to see field-level mapping.
     Motion character: Data packets animate through the pipeline on a 6s loop; the anonymization gate has a brief flash when a packet passes through it.
  7. Advisor Share & Commit — purpose: Convert the moment into a longitudinal behavior contract co-owned with the advisor.
     Primary element: Teams share preview with embedded Power BI report card, Sam's commitment slider (1-8 SMEs/week), and a 6-week cadence preview.
     Motion character: Share preview rises from bottom sheet with spring physics; commitment slider locks with a soft 'click' animation.
  8. Weekly Check-in Card (Friday) — purpose: Maintain the forecast contract as a recurring Teams ritual.
     Primary element: Compact Teams adaptive card: actual mix vs target ring, this week's delta, one Copilot-generated encouragement or course-correction line.
     Motion character: Ring fills on render; if drift is detected, a gentle amber pulse (never red, never punitive).
  9. FERPA Anonymization Disclosure — purpose: Make the privacy contract visible and inspectable, not buried in a footer.
     Primary element: Full-screen disclosure with the k-anonymity threshold (k≥15), what fields are used, what fields are never shown, and a 'See the data mapping' link to the dataflow screen.
     Motion character: Sections expand accordion-style with restrained 200ms easing; no decorative motion — the gravity is the point.
  10. Advisor Caseload Dashboard — purpose: Give advisors a cohort-level view of which first-years match the high-risk brand-only pattern.
     Primary element: Caseload list of 38 first-years with risk band, current mix, and a 'Send Counterfactual' bulk action.
     Motion character: Risk bands render as soft pastels with no alarm coloring; bulk-send confirmation is a quiet bottom-toast.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) — every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Cohort Outcome Forecaster
     User action: Sam opens the Two Futures experience.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Sam's anonymized first-week behavior vector (major, GPA band, application count, application company-tier distribution) + 5 years of NUworks placement records (anonymized at k≥15).
     Output: Two cohort trajectories with placement rate, median offer band, ghosting median, application volume — JSON consumed by Power BI canvas.
     User benefit: Sam sees his probable future grounded in real peer outcomes, not generic advice.
  2. Counterfactual Narrative Writer (HEADLINE)
     User action: Sam scrolls into either cohort panel.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Cohort statistics + Sam's major + the delta between his current strategy and the cohort's strategy.
     Output: 2-3 sentence editorial summary of what the cohort's sophomore fall typically feels like, written in second-person, never reproducing source quotes verbatim. Uses Verbalized Sampling (k=3 with probabilities) so the displayed variant feels chosen, not generated.
     User benefit: Sam emotionally registers the contrast — not just numerically — and feels addressed rather than analyzed.
  3. Alumni Vignette Synthesizer (Anonymized)
     User action: Sam reaches the vignette carousel.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7 + Wiki RAG for industry context on SME categories
     Input: Clustered anonymized alumni records (k≥15 per cluster) + industry context for the SME types in the cluster.
     Output: Three 4-frame vignettes with synthetic monograms, no identifying details, with frame captions averaging 18 words each.
     User benefit: Statistical clusters become readable peer stories Sam can map himself onto.
  4. Portfolio Mix Recommender
     User action: Sam drags the brand/SME dial.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Current dial position + Sam's matched cohort's conditional outcome surface.
     Output: Live placement %, median offer band, ghosting count for the current mix; recommended inflection-point mix highlighted as a magnetic detent on the dial.
     User benefit: Sam discovers the lift comes from rebalancing, not abandoning brand names — making the change feel rational, not punitive.
  5. Sensitivity Analysis Explainer
     User action: Sam taps 'Why did the number move?'
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Decomposition of the placement-rate lift by input variable.
     Output: Ranked plain-English explanations: 'Adding 3 SME applications/week drives most of the lift because diversity reduces ghosting risk by 41%.'
     User benefit: Sam knows exactly which lever to pull, not just that levers exist.
  6. Advisor Caseload Pattern Detector
     User action: Advisor opens her sidebar.
     Model: Embeddings + Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: First-year cohort week-6 behavior vectors clustered against historical brand-only-risk archetype.
     Output: Ranked list of students whose pattern resembles the high-risk cluster, with confidence score.
     User benefit: Advisors spend their limited time on the students most likely to benefit from intervention.
  7. Imagen Editorial Silhouettes
     User action: Splash screen loads for any student.
     Model: Gemini Imagen
     Input: Prompt for two abstract, non-photorealistic silhouettes evoking divergent futures, color-graded to the editorial palette.
     Output: Two silhouette images rendered into the splash hero.
     User benefit: The moment feels designed for Sam, not templated — visual gravity matches the emotional stakes.
  8. Weekly Copilot Nudge Author
     User action: Friday cadence trigger fires in Teams.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Sam's actual application data this week + his locked-in commitment + tone calibration (encouraging, never punitive).
     Output: One adaptive-card line: either celebration ('You hit 5/4 SMEs this week — your forecast just moved to 71%') or course-correction ('Two days left to hit your 4 — here are three roles your forecast loves').
     User benefit: The forecast stays alive as a weekly relationship, not a one-time visualization.

SEED DATA — generate the FULL count of records per entity (not 1-3 example shapes — the actual full set):
  PRIMARY ENTITIES (3):
    • AnonymizedAlumniTrajectory — target_count 30
      Shape: {cluster_id, major, gpa_band, strategy_label, year_one_apps, year_one_brand_share, sophomore_placement_rate, median_offer_band, ghosting_count_median, time_to_offer_days, dominant_sme_categories, junior_year_brand_conversion_rate, vignette_synthetic_monogram}
      Example records summary: 5-year historical placement records, anonymized to k≥15 clusters, covering industrial engineering, business, computer science, and bioengineering majors across brand-only, brand-heavy, balanced, and SME-heavy strategies.
    • FirstYearStudentProfile — target_count 28
      Shape: {student_id, name_first, major, college, gpa_band, week6_app_count, week6_brand_share, matched_cluster_id, current_forecast_placement_pct, locked_commitment_smes_per_week, forecast_history[], advisor_assigned}
      Example records summary: Current first-years in the pilot with their week-6 application behavior, matched cohort assignment, current forecast values, and commitment status.
    • NUworksRoleListing — target_count 26
      Shape: {role_id, employer, employer_tier, role_title, major_fit[], skills_required[], historical_first_year_placement_rate, sme_quality_score, location, posted_date}
      Example records summary: Live open roles in NUworks the forecaster references for the 'roles your forecast loves' nudge, spanning brand-name and SME with metadata for the matcher.
  SECONDARY ENTITIES (4):
    • AdvisorCaseload — target_count 12
      Shape: {advisor_id, advisor_name, caseload_size, brand_only_risk_count, last_review_date}
      Example records summary: Co-op advisors with their first-year caseloads and current at-risk student counts.

    • DataflowMappingNode — target_count 11
      Shape: {node_id, system_name, node_type, fields_in[], fields_out[], anonymization_applied, owner_role}
      Example records summary: Nodes in the NUworks → Power Automate → Azure OpenAI → Power BI → Teams dataflow with field-level mappings.
    • AlumniVignette — target_count 12
      Shape: {vignette_id, cluster_id, synthetic_monogram, frame1_caption, frame2_caption, frame3_caption, frame4_caption, junior_year_outcome}
      Example records summary: Pre-synthesized vignettes (4 frames each) drawn from anonymized clusters, ready for carousel rendering.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Data-narrative editorial gravitas. Cinematic split-screen composition. Soft, low-contrast data viz reminiscent of FiveThirtyEight long-reads crossed with Apple Numbers' restraint. NYT The Upshot for higher ed. No corporate dashboard chrome. Microsoft Teams chrome present at the frame but never dominant — the canvas is editorial.
  Hero treatment: Full-bleed split-screen with the student's name set in a 56pt editorial serif (Tiempos or Source Serif), paired with a 14pt grotesque caption (Inter). Two ghosted silhouettes — abstract, non-photoreal, charcoal-on-cream gradient — breathe slowly on a 1.2s loop. The diagonal seam between them is a single 1px rule that animates inward when the user taps, not a heavy divider. Subtle NUworks data-source attribution lives bottom-left in 11pt, always visible, never apologetic.
  Motion character: Restrained, weighty, deliberate. Easing curves are cubic-out or spring-physics (stiffness 200, damping 22), never bouncy. Number transitions tween over 240ms — long enough to feel inevitable, short enough not to drag. Nothing flashes red, nothing scolds, nothing celebrates with confetti. The Friday check-in 'you hit your target' moment is a single quiet check mark, not a party. The aesthetic borrows from financial forecasting tools, not gamified ed-tech.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these — the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen prompt: 'Two abstract human silhouettes in charcoal-on-cream gradient, facing slightly away from each other, evoking divergent futures without faces or identifying features, editorial newspaper-illustration style, soft cross-hatching texture'
    2. Imagen prompt: 'A minimal walking-figure illustration in side profile, charcoal silhouette on cream, suitable for animation along a morphing path, editorial woodcut aesthetic'
    3. Imagen prompt: 'An abstract editorial illustration of two diverging paths through a stylized landscape, low contrast, watercolor-wash background, no text, evoking a fork in time rather than space'
    4. Imagen prompt: 'A textured paper background with subtle deckle edges, suitable as the canvas behind the Cohort Comparison dashboard, cream tone, editorial document gravitas'
    5. Imagen prompt: 'Three abstract monogram portraits (A, B, C) in matched style — single-letter editorial illustrations evoking three unnamed alumni, charcoal and soft ochre, no facial features'
    6. Imagen prompt: 'A schematic illustration of a data pipeline rendered in editorial-illustration style, with nodes for NUworks, Power Automate, Azure OpenAI, Power BI, and Teams, hand-drawn aesthetic, cream background, charcoal lines, soft data packets moving along the path'

FEATURE ROADMAP (4 phases) — the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3) — Foundations — Data Pipeline & Anonymization
     • Establish read-only Power Automate connection to NUworks placement history tables
     • Build anonymization gate enforcing k≥15 clustering with FERPA officer sign-off
     • Stand up Azure OpenAI proxy with Claude + Gemini multi-provider fallback
     • Ship the Underlying NUworks Data Map screen as the audit artifact
     • Pre-cluster 5 years of placements into 24 archetype clusters across 4 majors
     Success: FERPA officer signs off on dataflow; 24 clusters validated by Strategic Co-op Director.
  2. Phase 2 (Weeks 4-7) — Intelligence — Forecaster & Narrative Layer
     • Train Cohort Outcome Forecaster against held-out alumni placements; target >0.7 AUC
     • Author Counterfactual Narrative Writer prompts with Verbalized Sampling (k=3)
     • Build Alumni Vignette Synthesizer with k≥15 anonymization enforcement
     • Ship Two Futures Splash, Cohort Comparison, and Vignette Carousel screens
     • Run advisor design review with Liz; iterate copy tone (encouraging, never punitive)
     Success: Forecaster matches historical sophomore placement within ±8pp on held-out validation set.
  3. Phase 3 (Weeks 8-11) — Interaction — Live Adjuster & Commit Loop
     • Ship Live Portfolio Mix Adjuster with sub-300ms forecast updates
     • Wire Sensitivity Drilldown
     • Build Advisor Share & Commit flow and weekly Teams adaptive card cadence
     • Configure Power Automate Friday check-in schedule
     • Pilot with 40 first-year IE and Business students opted in via Liz's office
     Success: 70% of piloted students adjust their dial; 50% lock a commitment; 60% return for week-10 revisit.
  4. Phase 4 (Months 4-6) — Scale — Advisor Caseload & Cross-Major Expansion
     • Ship Advisor Caseload Dashboard with risk-pattern detector
     • Expand to Khoury and Bouvé first-years
     • Add longitudinal forecast revisits at weeks 6, 10, 14
     • Power BI executive dashboard for Liz showing cohort-level SME application shift
     • Quarterly FERPA audit and anonymization re-validation
     Success: First-year SME application volume up 35%; brand-only-share down 15pp at cohort level.

NARRATIVE ARC (8 beats) — the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Sam taps the Teams card titled 'Two versions of your sophomore year, Sam.' The splash renders his name in editorial serif beside two breathing silhouettes.
     AI: Forecaster has already matched his week-6 vector against 24 clusters and pre-rendered both panels; Imagen has generated his personalized silhouettes overnight.
     Feeling: Curiosity tinged with mild defensiveness — 'is this about me?'
  2. Minute 3
     User: Sam reads the brand-only cohort's 31% placement rate. He pauses. He has assumed he was in the 90%.
     AI: Narrative Writer renders the cohort summary in second person without verbatim quotes, calibrated to factual-not-scolding tone.
     Feeling: Quiet recalibration. The number is doing the work, not the copy.
  3. Minute 6 (THE AHA)
     User: Sam drags the dial from 100/0 toward 60/40. The placement counter climbs 31 → 47 → 63 → 78%. A walking alumni avatar morphs paths alongside him.
     AI: Mix Recommender streams conditional probabilities in real time; Sensitivity Explainer pre-stages the 'why' captions for the magnetic detent at 60/40.
     Feeling: Visceral. He didn't read this — he felt it move.
  4. Day 1 (afternoon)
     User: Sam shares the forecast with his advisor Maya and locks a commitment of 4 SMEs per week for 6 weeks.
     AI: Claude drafts a one-line opener for Sam's note based on his longest dwell (Sensitivity Drilldown — 47 seconds).
     Feeling: Resolve, with a hint of vulnerability. He's told someone.
  5. Week 1
     User: Friday Teams card: 'You hit 5/4 SMEs this week, Sam. Your forecast just moved to 44%.'
     AI: Power Automate pulls Sam's actual NUworks applications; Forecaster re-runs; Copilot composes the celebration line.
     Feeling: Tangible competence. The model is reflecting him back.
  6. Week 4
     User: Sam re-opens the experience voluntarily after a Formlabs interview lands. The week-6 vs week-10 overlay shows his forecast climbed to 64%.
     AI: Forecast history renders as a soft ascending line; Narrative Writer marks the inflection.
     Feeling: Ownership. He moved the number himself.
  7. Month 3
     User: Sam accepts a Formlabs co-op offer for sophomore fall. He texts Marcus, who texts Priya, who opens her own Counterfactual experience that night.
     AI: Advisor Caseload detector silently removes Sam from Maya's at-risk list; Liz's executive dashboard ticks first-year SME applications +6%.
     Feeling: Quiet confidence. The hyper-fixation has dissolved into agency.
  8. Month 6+
     User: Liz reviews the cohort dashboard with Jen: SME applications up 35%, brand-only-share down 15pp, advisor 1:1 quality scores up, no FERPA incidents.
     AI: Quarterly anonymization re-validation passes; pattern detector retrains on the new cohort.
     Feeling: Institutional vindication. The intervention worked without a new platform.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (12 beats) — the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Sam taps the Teams adaptive card 'Two versions of your sophomore year, Sam.'
     System: Teams hands off to embedded web view; splash screen prefetches both cohort datasets in the background.
     Motion/feedback: Card flips with a 360ms 3D rotation; web view fades in beneath. (360ms)
  2. Sam reads his name and watches two ghosted silhouettes breathe on the splash.
     System: Imagen-rendered silhouettes hold a 1.2s slow-breathing loop; CTA 'Show me both futures' fades in after 800ms.
     Motion/feedback: Silhouettes scale 1.00 → 1.03 → 1.00 on a sine ease. (1200ms)
  3. Sam taps 'Show me both futures.'
     System: Diagonal seam animates inward, splitting the screen; left panel renders Brand-Only cohort, right renders Balanced cohort.
     Motion/feedback: Numbers count up over 900ms with cubic-out easing; gauges sweep counter-rotationally. (900ms)
  4. Sam scrolls past the cohort dashboards into the Alumni Vignette Carousel.
     System: Three vignette cards parallax-slide in; first card auto-focuses; FERPA seal renders at carousel base.
     Motion/feedback: Parallax depth: background lags 30%; cards arrive on staggered 80ms intervals. (720ms)
  5. Sam taps 'What if I shifted my mix?'
     System: Live Portfolio Mix Adjuster screen transitions in; dial initializes at his current 100/0; counters above show 31% placement, $22-26/hr median, 6 ghosting events.
     Motion/feedback: Page slide with spring physics (stiffness 200, damping 22); dial pulses once to signal interactivity. (540ms)
  6. Sam begins dragging the dial leftward toward more SMEs.
     System: Mix Recommender streams new conditional outcomes every 80ms; counters tween smoothly; the walking alumni avatar morphs its path.
     Motion/feedback: Counter values tween 240ms each; path Bezier interpolates; subtle micro-bounce on dial increments. (240ms)
  7. Sam crosses the 60/40 inflection point.
     System: Magnetic detent grabs the dial briefly; placement counter flashes 78% with a restrained 1-frame highlight; Sensitivity Drilldown bars auto-render below.
     Motion/feedback: Dial haptic-style micro-bounce; counter brief 200ms scale to 1.06 then return. (200ms)
  8. Sam reads the sensitivity captions: 'Adding 3 SME applications/week drives most of the lift because diversity reduces ghosting risk by 41%.'
     System: Captions fade in below their lever bars in 80ms stagger.
     Motion/feedback: Lever bars fill left-to-right; captions slide up 8px on fade. (80ms)
  9. Sam taps 'Lock in my new mix.'
     System: Modal rises from bottom sheet proposing 4 SMEs/week × 6 weeks; advisor share toggle enabled by default.
     Motion/feedback: Bottom sheet spring-rises; commitment slider snaps with a soft 'click' animation. (420ms)

=== CONSULTING BRIEF (every field below is mandatory grounding for the prototype) ===
Thesis: Actively combats brand-name hyper-fixation by scraping NUworks for high-quality SME roles and pushing them to first-year students via Teams.
Description (what gets built):
First-year undergraduate students arrive with rigid expectations, fixating on massive tech companies and ignoring the vast majority of available roles at small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs). This concept uses a Power Automate crawler to continuously scan the existing NUworks database for high-quality, non-brand-name opportunities. An Azure OpenAI layer evaluates the job descriptions against the student's declared major and early interests, rewriting the dry job descriptions into engaging, value-focused summaries. These hidden gems are then pushed directly to the student via a weekly Microsoft Teams digest. By proactively surfacing these roles in a surface the student already checks, the university broadens their aperture and prevents the massive disappointment of failing to secure a top-tier placement.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students simply do not know what they do not know. As detailed in Theme 14, they lack the tools to discover high-quality SME opportunities. By bringing these roles directly to them, the tool reduces the anxiety of the search and prevents the self-sabotage of only applying to the top 1% of employers.
How it supports first-year undergraduate students outcomes over 18-24 months:
Broadening the search aperture early drastically improves the overall placement rate. When students apply to a balanced portfolio of employers, they secure interviews faster, experience less 'ghosting,' and ultimately match with roles that provide foundational skills, setting them up for greater success in subsequent co-op cycles.
Execution within Northeastern University's existing stack (named systems, connectors, AI layer location):
This solution leverages Power Automate to scrape or access via API the existing NUworks platform (which remains the system of record). Azure OpenAI processes the text, and Microsoft Teams acts as the delivery mechanism. It completely avoids the need to build a new 'job board' frontend, relying instead on automated, asynchronous communication through existing channels.
Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, Power Automate, Power BI fit (named tools that reduce cost/burden):
This fits Jen's mandate perfectly by utilizing Power Automate as the integration tissue between the legacy system (NUworks) and the modern communication surface (Teams). It avoids the cost of procuring specialized third-party job discovery platforms by building a lightweight workflow using existing licenses.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a statistical forecaster. Match the student's week-6 behavior vector against 5 years of anonymized NUworks placement records to project two cohort trajectories.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Student Vector: Major={major}, GPA={gpa_band}, Apps={week6_app_count}, BrandShare={week6_brand_share}. Return JSON with placement rate, median offer, ghosting median for Brand-Only vs Balanced cohorts.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an editorial writer for a higher-ed publication. Summarize cohort statistics into a 2-3 sentence second-person narrative. Tone: factual, encouraging, never scolding. Use Verbalized Sampling (k=3).
ai_flows.user_message_template: Write a summary for the {strategy_label} cohort in {major}. Stats: {placement_rate} placement, {ghosting} ghosting events. Do not use verbatim quotes.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a synthesizer of anonymized student stories. Create 4-frame vignettes from clustered records (k>=15). Never surface identifiable patterns.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Synthesize 3 vignettes for {major} students who took the {strategy_label} path. Include industry context for SME types.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a probability engine. Compute the conditional probability surface for a student's placement based on their portfolio mix.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Current Mix: {brand_pct}% Brand / {sme_pct}% SME. Return projected placement %, median offer, and ghosting count.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a data explainer. Decompose the placement-rate lift by input variable and explain it in plain English.

critique.summary: The prototype successfully implements the core counterfactual reveal and portfolio rebalancing interactions with strong adherence to the design system and AI requirements. However, it contains blocking violations: an `alert()` call in the Advisor Caseload screen, several buttons lacking `onClick` handlers, and references to an unimported `lucide` icon library that will cause runtime crashes. These have been fixed in the refined code.

issues.description: The Advisor Caseload screen uses `alert()` to simulate a toast notification.
issues.fix: Replace `alert()` with a state-driven toast notification.

issues.description: Several buttons (Dismiss, Update NUworks sync, View FERPA Disclosure) lack onClick handlers.
issues.fix: Wire all buttons to real state transitions or remove them.

issues.description: The code uses `lucide.*` components without importing the Lucide library, which will cause ReferenceErrors.

research_goal: Identify a comprehensive new strategy for co-op based on the current statement of work for NU, prior projects with NU, and fresh industry analysis of experiential learning and co-op engagement tactics to improve learner's chances of gaining meaningful experiential learning opportunities from pre-enrollment to graduate school
